title: Single-key shortcuts, message filtering, and two new commands
notes: Single-key shortcuts: every command can now also be bound to a bare key — plain s, g, Shift+G — in the new Single key column on the options page. It sits alongside the normal shortcut instead of replacing it, and stays quiet while you are typing in a text field.

New /filter command: filters the message list of the folder you are already looking at, live as you type. /body and /recipients — or Ctrl+B and Ctrl+R while typing — widen the fields it searches, and a bare /filter clears it again.
While filtering, the popup shrinks to just the input and moves to the bottom-right corner of the Thunderbird window, so the message list it is filtering stays visible.
New /go command: jump straight to an account's inbox from the popup.
New /columns command: show or hide the columns of the message list (Date, Sender, Size, …) without leaving the popup.
New option: recreate the search window each time instead of keeping it minimized, so it leaves no lingering taskbar entry between uses.
Fixed: pressing a search shortcut while the search window was already open could open a second window instead of focusing the existing one.
Fixed: the search window could only ever grow when fitting itself to its content, never shrink.
Fixed: saving on the options page could discard settings that have no checkbox of their own.
